lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano, soft and spacious]

[Verse 1: warm, quiet, piano only]
Taxi at the kerb at five, the house was still asleep
Gate nineteen, a paper cup, a lanyard and a beep
There's a drawing in my pocket of a dog that's mostly green
I'm thirty thousand feet above the best thing I have seen

[Chorus: band lifts in, slide guitar, stacked harmonies]
I come around once every night
A face on a screen in the kitchen light
Say goodnight, blow a kiss to the glass
I'm a satellite dad
Going over, going past
Look up, I'm the slow one, I'm the last

[Verse 2: warm, bass and brushed drums]
The minibar is humming and the curtains never close
I've a slide deck and a rental and a town that no one knows
I tell myself it's for them, and mostly that is true
But a year's a lot of bedtimes to be waving at a view

[Chorus: band, slide guitar, stacked harmonies]
I come around once every night
A face on a screen in the kitchen light
Say goodnight, blow a kiss to the glass
I'm a satellite dad
Going over, going past
Look up, I'm the slow one, I'm the last

[Bridge: synth swoops, acoustic guitar, voice higher]
And nobody tells you
That the signal isn't you
It's a picture of a person
Coming through

[Final Chorus: full band, voices wide, slide guitar soaring]
I come around once every night
A face on a screen in the kitchen light
Say goodnight, blow a kiss to the glass
I'm a satellite dad
Going over, going past
Look up, I'm the slow one, I'm the last

[Outro: voices repeating, band fading, a door opening]
I'm coming down
I'm coming down
I'm home
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 68 BPM, 4/4, B-flat major. Slow, floating and lonely, with a chorus that rises like a launch.

VOICE: Male tenor, warm and conversational in the verses with a slight Southern-English-American drawl. In the chorus his voice is stacked several times and joined by high harmony voices, so it seems to widen. A higher, more exposed sound in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A grand piano with gentle, rolling chords. A slide guitar playing long, rising swoops in the chorus. An early synthesiser making soft, sliding space sounds. Acoustic guitar strums. A melodic electric bass. Brushed drums in the verses, a soft full kit in the choruses.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:49 Chorus 1, the band lifts in. 1:24 Verse 2. 1:59 Chorus 2. 2:34 Bridge with synth swoops. 2:52 Final chorus. 3:27 Outro, the voices repeat a new line as the band fades, then a door opens and one last line is sung plainly at 4:08.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1970s singer-songwriter rock: warm, spacious and analogue, piano and voice in front, the chorus wide with voices and slide guitar.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The slide guitar's first rising swoop as the chorus begins at 0:49.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original astronaut stays in orbit. This one comes down: the outro is a new line the 1972 song does not have, and a front door. The bridge ('the signal isn't you') could only have been written in the age of video calls.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Loneliness, guilt, realisation, coming home.
